title: The Gas Station You Drive Past Every Day Is a Photograph Waiting for Night
excerpt: Fstoppers argues daylight documents a place while night light transforms it, and that darkness is the best background remover a photographer has. Expose for the highlights, set the white balance by hand, and scout without the camera.

title: The One Slider Move That Makes a Sunset Glow in Lightroom
excerpt: Fstoppers follows Christian Möhrle's sunset edit: raising blacks inside a feathered mask creates the glow that exposure would blow out, while restrained color and a low denoise setting keep the file clean. The trick copies what a diffusion filter does, without the commitment.

title: Your Camera's Sensor Is Colorblind. Here Is How It Fakes Color
excerpt: Fstoppers explains that every photosite on your sensor is a grayscale light meter, and color arrives through a 1975 Kodak patent: the Bayer mosaic, half green to match human vision. Demosaicing then rebuilds two-thirds of every pixel, which is why raw files look different in every converter.
